Performance follow-up after issue #104 / merged PR #107

Implementation review: one gpt-6-astra and two gpt-5.6-sol agents independently
examined common decoder allocations, scanner/helper reuse, and access projection
quality. Each implemented a separately owned change with regression tests.

Adversarial review of e6d0462721d8e5e5caf167665738bce5bf3c605a:
- gpt-6-astra correctness: clean after historical event-ID, independent event
  ownership, static precedence, empty-field shape, and CaptureInto regressions.
- gpt-6-astra security: clean after 42,597 historical logfmt differential cases,
  177,156 numeric grammar cases, binary values, metadata, redaction, and WAL tests.
- gpt-5.6-sol efficiency/quality/API: clean; compiler analysis confirmed that the
  caller's small capture array remains on the stack. No shared scratch state.

All three reviewers re-reviewed final source revision
a64e0e7abf4585ed520afa0bf53098dd3a6f86a3 and returned clean results:
- Astra correctness: unchanged framing error precedence, controls rejected on
  both logfmt paths, Docker string ownership, and exactly equivalent bounded
  access timestamp comparison. Targeted collector/parserconfig/jsonnumber pass.
- Astra security: historical differential, strict timestamp spelling, Docker
  validation/ownership, redaction, and reparsing tests pass. Initial broad test
  selection failed to bind loopback sockets in the sandbox; the parent's full
  elevated tests, race tests, and compiled backend integrations passed.
- Sol efficiency/quality/API: owned Docker stream reuse is safe; AppendFormat's
  canonical buffer and Java capture buffer remain on the stack; logfmt avoids
  redundant control scanning for escaped strings without weakening validation.
  Targeted collector/parserconfig/jsonnumber tests pass.

No actionable findings remained on the final source revision. Reviewers did not
run timing benchmarks during the final measurement. Regression files added by
reviewers are retained in the repository and run in the ordinary test suites.

Supplemental malformed benchmark investigation:
The 200ms samples showed a noisy large-logfmt slowdown and a small large-NGINX
slowdown. An Astra agent disassembled the existing baseline/final benchmark
binaries with llvm-objdump. The ordinary-byte logfmt quoted scan has identical
instruction operations/count; the new escape flag is written only on the
backslash branch that this fixture never takes. Scanner.value has exactly 237
instructions in both binaries; the normalized differences are four metadata
addresses, with identical loop instructions. Successful field projection is
not reached by these malformed inputs. No added scan work, new spill, or source
fix was identified. No source edits or timing tests were made by the reviewer.
The disassembly is retained in profiles/*-asm.txt. The parent then scheduled
20 longer one-second paired samples for the two affected cases.
